fields.h1: Build a Photography Order Form That Sorts and Totals Every Order
fields.hero_description: Build a photography order form that prices each package, tags it with the class or team, and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Settles Before Anything Prints
fields.features_subheading: Each question settles a detail you would otherwise chase by email after the shoot, and the lab gets the right image at the right size.
fields.feature_1:
Packages priced before anyone picks

Each package on the form lists the prints inside it and what it costs. A parent can weigh a sheet of wallets against an 8x10 package and choose without calling the studio.
fields.feature_2:
Names that match the face in the frame

The form asks for the subject's name plus the detail you sort by, like a homeroom or jersey number. Each order points to one child, even when two children share a first name.
fields.feature_3:
Only the sizes your lab prints

You list the print sizes your lab offers, such as 5x7, 8x10 and 16x20, with the finishes for each. Customers pick from that list instead of typing a size the lab lacks.
fields.feature_4:
An alert as each order lands

The app sends you an email or Slack alert for every new order, with the name and package on the first line. Customers can get a reminder before the order window closes.
fields.feature_5:
Orders kept in a database you own

Every order saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps on a busy picture day. Filter the rows by class or by team, and the list for your lab is done.
fields.feature_6:
Export the code when a developer asks

On paid plans, the full code of the form and its order database exports to your GitHub repository. A developer can host it beside your studio's website or extend it later.

fields.usecase_heading: Order Forms for Four Kinds of Shoot
fields.tab_content_1:
Ms. Wilder's class gets its prints in one stack

Bramblecrest Portraits photographs a whole elementary school on picture day. Fenna Basu orders Package B for $34 for her son Rafferty, a 2nd grader in Ms. Wilder's class. The form files the order under his homeroom, and the studio packs that class's prints together.
fields.tab_content_2:
No guessing which player wears 9

Northpaw Sports Photo shoots a youth soccer league in one morning, team after team. Niko Ostrowski wears jersey 9 for the Hornbills U10 team. His parent picks the $28 team package and adds a $12 memory mate, and the shoot-day roster lists his $40 order beside the number 9.
fields.tab_content_3:
By image number, two prints and a canvas

Fernlight Studio shares a proof gallery after each family session, with a number under every frame. Mirela Prakash orders two 8x10 prints of image 112 at $22 each and a 16x20 canvas of image 87. The form adds the $145 canvas to her $44 in prints and shows a $189 total.
fields.tab_content_4:
Orders after day 10 ship home for $9

Lumen Hollow Photo shoots a dance recital and delivers prints to the dance studio at no charge for orders placed within 10 days of the show. Vesna Ilic orders a $45 print bundle on day 12. Shipping it to her home adds $9, for a $54 total.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Photography Order Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to turn your packages and print prices into a photography order form that totals each order.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every package and print size
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the detail you sort by
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the order window and delivery
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each package you sell with the prints inside it and its price. Add the single print sizes your lab makes, each with a price. This list becomes the order choices and lets the form total every order.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the one detail you sort by when prints come back from the lab, such as a homeroom teacher or a jersey number. The form asks for it on every order. Each set of prints then reaches the right child.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide when orders close and where finished prints go, whether to the school or to a home address. If late orders ship home for a fee, write down the fee and the day it starts.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a plain-English description of the form that names your packages with their prices, plus your delivery rules. Emergent builds a working form from that description, order totals included.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Change any rule with a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for each change in a sentence, such as a sibling package or a new canvas size. Emergent changes the form when you prompt it again. A new price list takes one line.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Place a test order as a parent
fields.howto_step_6_des: Order from the published form with two prints and a delivery after the studio window. Check that the total matches your price list and that the new-order alert reaches you.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link before the shoot
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send the form link home with the picture day flyer, or add it to the email that delivers a proof gallery. Orders then arrive in one table instead of in envelopes and inbox threads.

faq_plan.q: What is a photography order form?
faq_plan.a: A photography order form is the sheet or web form a customer fills in to buy prints from a shoot. It records who is in the photo, which package or print sizes they want, how many of each, and where the prints should go. You can send one home before picture day, or with a proof gallery after a portrait session.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a photography order form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: your packages and prices, the detail you sort orders by, and your delivery rules. Emergent builds a working form with order totals, and you change it later by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a picture order form ask for?
faq_plan.a: A picture order form should ask for the name of the person in the photo, the package or print sizes, and the quantity of each. Add the detail you sort by, such as a homeroom or a jersey number, and an image number field when customers pick from a gallery. Show the order total before the customer sends it.

faq_plan.q: What should I change first in an editable photography order form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with the packages and print sizes, and match them to what your lab prints. Then swap the template's sorting field for the one you use when prints come back, like a team name. If your orders need a rule the template cannot hold, such as a shipping fee after a deadline, build a custom order form instead. With Emergent, each later change is one prompt.

faq_plan.q: Is a free photography order form template enough for a whole school?
faq_plan.a: Not on its own: a free template gives you the fields, but you add up totals and sort orders by hand for every class. Build the form with your prices and sorting rules in it instead, and orders arrive grouped by homeroom with their totals already worked out.

faq_plan.q: What should a free sports photography order form template include?
faq_plan.ref: free sports photography order form template
faq_plan.secondary: free sports photography order form template
faq_plan.a: It should include the player's name, team, and jersey number, plus the package and any add-ons such as a memory mate. Add a parent's email for the order confirmation and the team's shoot time if several teams share one session. The jersey number is what ties an order to one player when two children on the field share a name.

faq_plan.q: How do I match each order on a sports photography order form to the right player?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the jersey number and team on every order, then print the roster sorted by team and number before the shoot. Check each player against the roster as they step up for the photo. If the league also collects kit sizes, put those on a separate uniform order form and keep the photo roster to names and numbers.

faq_plan.q: How should a photography order form handle siblings?
faq_plan.a: Let parents add a second child to the same order, each with a name and homeroom, and offer a sibling package if you photograph them together. Each child's prints then file under the right class, and the parent sends one order instead of two.

faq_plan.q: How do I send orders from a photography order form to my print lab?
faq_plan.a: Filter the orders by class or team and send the lab one list per batch, with every print size and quantity on it. An app built with Emergent keeps the orders in a database you own, and one filter produces that list. If your lab takes orders through an API, the app can connect to it and send them there.

faq_plan.q: Can a school use one photography order form for picture day and a fundraiser?
faq_plan.a: It can, but keep them on separate forms. Picture day orders need the student and the homeroom, while a fundraiser order form tracks which seller gets credit for each sale. Two forms give the photographer and the fundraiser lead each a clean list.
